title: Console Triage: Catalyst Sprint 21 Cutlist
content:
Purpose:
This document captures grooming decisions for the Console & Rollouts team ahead of Catalyst Sprint 21 (bridge sprint). It is a pragmatic cutlist for scope we will commit to, items deferred, and immediate follow-ups. Aim is to lock sprint scope by EOD 2026-06-10 so engineering can start scheduling infra and design handoffs.

Context / constraints:
- Sprint window: 2026-06-14 -> 2026-06-27 (2 weeks)
- Core focus: stabilize routing UI + rollout UX polish for Dedicated customers.
- Team capacity: 3 FE, 2 BE, 1 SRE on-call overlap, plus 1 product designer (partial).
- Hard must-deliver: RE-INF-3421 (rollout fallback behavior) due to enterprise pilot.

Triaged Cutlist (final decisions)
1) RE-INF-3421: Rollout fallback UX (KEEP - high)
   - Owner: Liam Chen
   - Estimate: 8 SP
   - Why: Enterprise pilot requires deterministic fallback visuals + clear failure state messaging.
   - Acceptance criteria: fallback toggle visible in rollout detail + automated retry CTA; unit tests for state transitions; telemetry event names documented.
   - Risk: backend contract changes from platform team — coordinate early.

2) RE-INF-3520: Token-level latency breakdown (KEEP - medium)
   - Owner: Ana Gomez
   - Estimate: 5 SP
   - Why: Important for debugging Dedicated perf regressions; MVP scoped to per-request histogram + small UI surface in trace view.
   - Acceptance criteria: histogram renders for requests > 100 tokens, sample rate documented, sampling toggle in debug toolbar.
   - Notes: defer heatmap/comparison features to next sprint.

3) Console: Quick-promote from canary to prod (CUT -> defer)
   - Owner: product (Maya)
   - Estimate: 8 SP (deferred)
   - Why cut: Not enough QA bandwidth this sprint; high risk for rollout regressions.
   - Next action: move to backlog slice for Sprint 22 and add exploratory test plan.

4) UX: Mini-rework of model selection dropdown (KEEP - low)
   - Owner: Ravi Singh
   - Estimate: 3 SP
   - Why: small friction noted in user tests; quick win to reduce wrong-model errors.
   - Acceptance criteria: add recent models header, keyboard navigation, A11y label.

5) Opt-in: Prefetch suggestion chips (CUT -> spike)
   - Owner: Design (Maya)
   - Estimate: 1 SP spike (research only)
   - Action: run 3-day spike to measure bandwidth and cache impact; no UI changes in sprint unless spike confirms low cost.

6) Observability: Per-route error breakdown in Console (CUT to next quarter)
   - Reason: Backend aggregation API not finalized; large scope.

7) Bugfix: permissions edge-case in rollout cloning (KEEP - critical small fix)
   - Owner: BE engineer
   - Estimate: 2 SP
   - Acceptance criteria: cloned rollout respects org-level role mappings; unit + integration test.

Wireframe / UX notes (quick sketches / handoff items)
- Rollout detail page: add a compact fallback state panel under status header. Content: brief reason text, last successful region, retry CTA. (See quick sketch in linked PR 612.)
- Latency histogram: place inside trace modal, collapsed by default. Width constrained to 360px, simplified tooltip with p50/p95.
- Model dropdown: reorder to show pinned models on top, add small chevron for long lists. Keyboard focus ring and sr-only labels required.

Backlog grooming rationale (how decisions made)
- Prioritized by: customer SLAs (pilot customers), implementation risk, QA cost, design effort, sequencing dependencies with platform infra.
- Cuts were chosen where cross-team coordination or incomplete infra would substantially increase risk of regressions.
- Small UX quality work (<=3 SP) kept as quick wins to maintain momentum and ship visible improvements.

Open questions / blockers
- Platform API: will routing fallback be exposed via /rollouts API change? (Action: Liam to sync with infra on 2026-06-07).
- Sampling config for latency histogram: needs SRE sign-off on storage/ingestion cost (Action: Ana to open quick SLO ticket).

Next steps / owners
- Liam: draft API contract + sample telemetry events by 2026-06-08.
- Ana: prototype histogram in storybook and push review PR by 2026-06-11.
- Maya: update release notes template to include rollout fallback copy, finalize canary promotion deferral to Sprint 22.
- Ravi: deliver model-dropdown spec with accessibility checklist by 2026-06-09.

Meeting cadence
- Quick sync (15m) Mon 2026-06-08 10:00 — unblock platform contract.
- Grooming follow-up (30m) Wed 2026-06-10 16:00 — finalize sprint board and assign tickets.

Appendix: quick decisions log (for audit)
- 2026-06-05 14:10 — Initial triage: identified RE-INF-3421 as high priority due to customer requirement (Maya).
- 2026-06-07 09:30 — Design/Eng alignment: agreed latency histogram MVP scope (Ana, Liam).
- 2026-06-09 11:20 — Final cutlist locked (this doc) ahead of sprint planning.

Notes to reviewer: this is a working doc. Add comments inline for scope pushback or if you think an item needs to move between KEEP/CUT. Mark critical blockers in Slack #console-rollouts so we can escalate.

End of doc.
